claims.text: AOF rewriting produces a new file containing the minimal operations needed to recreate the current data set rather than compressing the old append history.
For the pre-7.0 single-file flow, Redis continues appending during rewrite and appends the buffered increment to the rewritten result before switching files.
Since Redis 7.0, AOF data is split into multiple files in the configured append directory, so older single-file descriptions are version-specific.
Redis documents copy-on-write memory overhead during pre-7.0 AOF rewrite when writes continue, so fork and write pressure are capacity and latency boundaries rather than a claim of zero interruption.
The published AOF set is the recoverable state; operational backup guidance requires checking whether rewrite is in progress before copying the multi-part AOF directory.
